{{Short description|American ecological statistician}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=July 2021}}

[[File:Kathi Irvine USGS.jpg|thumb|Irvine in 2011]]
'''Kathryn Mary''' ('''Kathi''') '''Irvine''' is an American research statistician for the [[United States Geological Survey]] (USGS), affiliated with the Bozeman Environmental and Ecological Statistics Research Group, at the USGS Northern Rocky Mountain Science Center in [[Bozeman, Montana]].{{r|bees}} Her research involves [[environmental statistics]] including both the fundamentals of [[spatial statistics]] and its application to wildlife populations including [[bat]]s, [[pika]]s, [[elk]], [[pine tree]]s, and [[sagebrush steppe]]s.{{r|usgs}}

==Education and career==
Irvine majored in biology at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]]. She has a master's degree in ecology and environmental sciences from the [[University of Maine]], and a second master's degree and PhD in statistics from [[Oregon State University]], completed in 2007.{{r|usgs}} Her dissertation, ''Graphical models for multivariate spatial data'', was supervised by Alix Gitelman.{{r|diss}}

She became an assistant professor at [[Montana State University]] in 2008 before moving to the USGS in 2011.{{r|usgs}} Beyond the USGS, she is a member of the core planning team of the North American Bat Monitoring Program,{{r|nabat}} and maintains an affiliate faculty position in statistics at Montana State University.{{r|msu}}

==Service and recognition==
Irvine was the 2018 chair of the [[American Statistical Association]] (ASA) Section on Statistics and the Environment, has been president of the Montana Chapter of the ASA several times, and has been publications chair for the ASA Section on Government Statistics.{{r|2get}} She was named a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2021.{{r|fasa}}
